cohort: The study included 14,196 women who delivered singleton live infants at a maternal and child health hospital in Beijing, China, in 2012.
finding: High prepregnancy BMI or excessive gestational weight gain were associated with increased risks of adverse pregnancy outcomes including gestational diabetes, hypertensive disorders, postpartum hemorrhage, caesarean delivery, macrosomia, and large for gestational age, while inadequate gestational weight gain increased risks of preterm delivery, low birth weight, and small for gestational age.
mod_finding: Women with high prepregnancy BMI or excessive gestational weight gain had higher risks of caesarean delivery.
